name: Wolverine
summary: Short, grumpy and almost impossible to kill. Logan is the X-Men's clawed Canadian mutant, with a healing factor, animal senses and an unbreakable adamantium skeleton.
origin: Wolverine was introduced as a Canadian agent picking a fight with the Hulk, which is about the most Wolverine way to arrive. Roy Thomas wanted a Canadian hero, Len Wein wrote him, and John Romita Sr. designed the look for The Incredible Hulk #180–181 in 1974. A year later he joined the new X-Men and became their breakout star. His power is a healing factor that closes wounds fast and has kept him alive for well over a century, plus animal-sharp senses and claws that slide out of his forearms. A secret program bonded unbreakable adamantium to his skeleton, and the 2001 Origin series finally revealed he was born James Howlett in 19th-century Canada. Short, grumpy and hard to kill: the perfect antihero.

storyline.title: Canada's agent
storyline.beat: Wolverine appears in The Incredible Hulk #180–181 as a Canadian government agent sent to stop the Hulk and the Wendigo.

storyline.title: The new team
storyline.beat: He joins the new X-Men in Giant-Size X-Men #1 and slowly becomes the team's breakout star.

storyline.title: Claremont and Miller
storyline.beat: A four-issue limited series sends Logan to Japan to win back his love Mariko, defining his code of honour.

storyline.title: The adamantium process
storyline.beat: Barry Windsor-Smith shows the brutal secret program that bonded unbreakable adamantium to Logan's skeleton.

storyline.title: Bone claws
storyline.beat: Magneto rips out his adamantium, revealing that Wolverine's claws are actually bone.

storyline.title: James Howlett
storyline.beat: Logan's past is finally revealed: he was born James Howlett, a sickly rich boy in late 19th-century Canada.

storyline.title: Gone and back
storyline.beat: Wolverine dies encased in liquid adamantium in Death of Wolverine, and returns in 2018.

gossip.text: Wolverine's claws were always made of adamantium.
gossip.truth: A 1993 story revealed they are bone. The adamantium was bonded to his skeleton later.

gossip.text: Co-creator Len Wein first meant the claws to be part of Wolverine's gloves. Chris Claremont later made them part of his body.
His first full appearance was in The Incredible Hulk #181. Issue #180 ends with a one-panel cameo.
Wolverine didn't get an ongoing solo series until 1988, fourteen years after his debut.
Hugh Jackman played him from 2000 to 2017, then returned in Deadpool & Wolverine (2024).

quiz.q: Wolverine debuted in which hero's comic?
Who ripped the adamantium out of Wolverine?
How tall is Wolverine in the comics?
quiz.why: He is famously short, unlike Hugh Jackman.

timeline.title: Canada's agent
timeline.note: The Incredible Hulk #180 and #181 introduce a short, clawed Canadian sent to stop the Hulk.

timeline.title: Joining the new team
timeline.note: Giant-Size X-Men #1 recruits Logan into the new, global X-Men.

timeline.title: Claremont and Miller
timeline.note: A four-issue Wolverine series sends Logan to Japan, cementing his samurai-tough image.

timeline.title: Adamantium torn out
timeline.note: X-Men #25 has Magneto rip the metal from Logan's skeleton, revealing claws made of bone.

timeline.title: Hugh Jackman in X-Men
timeline.note: Bryan Singer's X-Men casts Hugh Jackman, starting a long run as Logan across many films.

timeline.title: Origin
timeline.note: The Origin miniseries finally reveals Logan's 19th-century past as James Howlett.

timeline.title: Death of Wolverine
timeline.note: A four-issue series kills Logan, encased in the very metal that made him.

timeline.title: Logan passes the torch
timeline.note: Logan sends Jackman's hero off in a grim western, with young Laura Kinney ready to carry the claws.
